notes: Two-slice toaster with three heating elements wired in parallel and four circuit boards: three inside the plastic cover and a fourth that carries the switch. The 35 ohm figure is the teardown author's own reading.

gaps: No wattage is recorded. Retailer listings say 800 W (Home Depot and manuals.plus), but both pages returned HTTP 403.
The 35 ohm figure per element is the teardown author's own reading, not checked against any rating, so it is not put in v, a or w.
The teardown describes no electromagnet, bimetal browning control or clockwork timer, so none of those template parts is claimed.
The guide has no parts list, so counts come from its step text (three boards inside the cover plus a fourth switch board).
The heating element type (nichrome, mica or other) is not stated in the guide.
'Extra-wide' and 'pop-up' in the researcher's model line were dropped: the teardown uses neither word.
Oster's catalogue status for this SKU appeared only in a search snippet and was not opened.
A manual for this exact model was not reachable. Manual copies on manualmachine.com and manuals.online returned HTTP 403, and the manualshive copy showed a bot check, which was not passed.
method: iFixit teardown guide 153633, Oster 2-Slice Toaster TSSTJC5BBK Disassembly (title names the model), read via /api/2.0/guides/153633 and the guide page. The guide is community-written, with no introduction or parts list; used for facts and links only.

Refused or unavailable: Home Depot product page (HTTP 403), manuals.plus product page (HTTP 403), manualmachine.com Oster manual (HTTP 403), manuals.online Oster manual (HTTP 403), Oster Salsify product pages (HTTP 404), manualshive copy (bot check, not passed).

comps.spec: Three heating elements (left, centre and right) wired in parallel. The teardown author gives each as 35 ohms, and the schematic it shows has 120 V AC reaching them only when the switch is pushed down
Three circuit boards attached to the inside of the plastic cover. They take input from the buttons and the dial

Mechanical switch on the fourth circuit board, connecting the current to the user interface and the heating elements. The user pushes it down and it is held mechanically; the cancel button releases it
Metal top and two metal side covers, held on by tabs. The top stays attached to a spring
Spring attached to the metal top; the guide detaches it from the metal tabs by pulling its hook out with pliers
